brewing.notes: A safe starting point for white tea: use hot but not boiling water and give it time.

description:
An old-arbor white tea from Mengku in Lincang, known as a pressed cake with leaf from Nuo Wu and Ba Wai villages.

Treat it as you would any white tea: hot but not boiling water, patient steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: One documented pressing uses first-flush spring 2024 leaf from two family gardens, aged two years before pressing. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Picked and processed by hand, sun-dried, then pressed at medium-plus compression.
appearance_dry: Usually downy buds or soft, silvery-green leaves.
appearance_liquor: Usually a pale straw to light amber.
appearance_wet: Usually soft, intact leaf and bud.
vintage_note: White teas are normally sold either fresh, from the current year, or pressed and aged for several years, with the year stated.
